forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.lead: Vacancies in core financial and audit functions, coupled with outsourcing of internal audit, weaken governance capacity and control oversight. This is significant during Local Government Reorganisation, which may compound organizational transition risks.

findings.headline: Core finance functions have ongoing staffing vacancies, with internal audit outsourcing planned for 2026/27
findings.detail: The Resources Department experienced a salary underspend of £84,213 primarily due to vacancies in Accounts, ICT and Audit sections. The council is setting aside £80,000 of this underspend in earmarked reserves to cover service continuity costs in 2026/27, specifically for internal audit services following planned outsourcing of the internal audit function. This indicates both ongoing staffing pressures and a structural change to governance functions.
findings.matters: Vacancies in core financial and audit functions, coupled with outsourcing of internal audit, weaken governance capacity and control oversight. This is significant during Local Government Reorganisation, which may compound organizational transition risks.
findings.figures: £84,213 salary underspend; £80k set aside in earmarked reserves
findings.quote: Mainly due to vacancies within the Accounts, Audit and ICT sections. £80k of the underspend has been set aside in earmarked reserves to support continuity of these services during the 2026/27 financial year, including outsourcing of the Internal Audit service.

findings.headline: EPR funding of £791,804 per annum may need adjustment as packaging volumes and scheme develop
findings.detail: The council is forecasting £791,804 EPR income annually (approximately £792k) and has assumed this continues in future years. However, the report warns: 'While Government has provided assurances around the scheme, the longer-term value remains a risk as packaging volumes and the scheme itself develop. The level of income allowed for in the forecast may need to be adjusted as further information becomes known.' This is a material income stream (4.4% of general fund) that may be unstable.
findings.matters: EPR is a new, developing scheme and the council is already factoring it into recurring budget assumptions. Loss or reduction of this income would force additional budget rebalancing in years when the £0.895m gap is already unaddressed.
findings.figures: 2026/27 EPR income: £791,804 (assumed recurring in future years)
findings.quote: While Government has provided assurances around the scheme, the longer-term value remains a risk as packaging volumes and the scheme itself develop.

findings.headline: Potential external borrowing needed if capital spending and LGR costs deplete cash faster than expected
findings.detail: The council currently has no external debt and has used internal resources (reserves) to finance its capital programme. However: 'If cash balances reduce more quickly than expected, external borrowing may be needed, which would impact the revenue forecast.' The approved four-year capital programme is £16.962m (£12.860m in 2026/27 alone), financed by reserves and balances. The report suggests that the council should 'review existing schemes for deliverability, affordability and relevance' rather than invite new bids, signalling concern about cash adequacy.
findings.matters: A lender needs to know whether a council can finance its capital programme without recourse to borrowing. The report's language ('may be needed') indicates this is uncertain and could tip from possibility to necessity quickly. Any external borrowing will add revenue costs at a time when the revenue budget is already in deficit.
findings.figures: Capital programme 2026/27–2029/30: £16.962m; £12.860m in 2026/27; £1.322m internal borrowing assumed 2026/27
findings.quote: If cash balances reduce more quickly than expected, external borrowing may be needed, which would impact the revenue forecast.

findings.headline: First-quarter 2026/27 overspend of £129k suggests the current year may not balance unless corrected
findings.detail: As of end-June 2026, the council shows a net adverse variance of £129,249 (4.27%) against the original budget. Key drivers: Housing Benefits £423k adverse, Trade Waste income £32k adverse (described as 'likely to be the outturn position unless new contracts are secured'), planning appeals consultant costs £38k adverse. If this variance runs pro-rata for the full year, the 2026/27 outturn overspend would be approximately £516k, far exceeding the £277k planned drawdown from balances.
findings.matters: A first-quarter variance this large, driven in part by structural income shortfalls (Trade Waste) rather than one-off items, raises questions about budget realism. If 2026/27 closes with a material unplanned overspend, reserves will be drawn down faster than forecast, worsening the cash position ahead of 2027/28.
findings.figures: Q1 net variance: £129,249 (4.27%); Housing Benefits adverse £423k; Trade Waste adverse £32k; planning appeals adverse £38k
findings.quote: For the first quarter, there shows a net overspend/under recovery of income of £129,249. Positive amounts are adverse and negative amounts are favourable unless otherwise stated.

findings.headline: Interest income falling from £788k to £440k despite current Bank Rate of 3.75%, driven by capital-spending and LGR depletion of cash
findings.detail: The council previously benefited from higher investment income. Even though Bank Rate sits at 3.75%, the forecast income is dropping sharply: from £787,980 in 2026/27 to £440,000 in 2027/28 (a £348k hit in one year). The reason: 'Due to heavy investment through the capital programme, largely funded by the Council's earmarked reserves and general fund balances, this substantially reduces the monies available for investment.' This signals that the council's cash buffer is being rapidly consumed by capital spending and LGR costs.
findings.matters: Interest income does not solve any budget problem; it merely masks the underlying deficit. A council burning reserves to fund capital while facing a structural revenue gap is on an unsustainable path. The drop in available cash is a leading indicator of reserve depletion.
findings.quote: Due to heavy investment through the capital programme, largely funded by the Council's earmarked reserves and general fund balances, this substantially reduces the monies available for investment.
